basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5.' and it opens 'Vers. 5. Numera stellas. Sic erit semen tuum. Gemina species ostenditur seminis Abrahae.'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 5. Numera stellas. Sic erit semen tuum. Gemina species ostenditur seminis Abrahae. Nam superius dixit: Erit semen tuum sicut arena maris. Hic vero dicit: Sic erit semen tuum sicut stellae coeli, quia in illa plebe quidam futuri erant carnales et terreni, qui arenae comparantur, aridi, infecundi a bonis operibus, alii vero spiritales et coelestes, virtutum splendore fulgentes, quos stellis coeli comparat.
